ApiError.description:

`error` is an open, stable machine-readable code; `docUrl` links to its documentation and
`retryable` says whether an unchanged request may succeed later. `message` is for people,
not matching. `timestamp` is RFC 3339 UTC; optional `requestId` mirrors `X-Request-Id`.
Optional `next` describes recovery and `details` carries code-specific information.
Handle known codes and fall back on the HTTP status for unknown ones.

jurisdiction, KYB status, and regulatory licences — the "who is the other
side and are they authorised" a compliance officer needs. Router/bridge
routes settle through a protocol (CCTP, Relay, …), not a VASP counterparty:
those report `counterparty_type = "protocol"` with no jurisdiction/licences,
which is itself the compliance-relevant fact (no VASP-to-VASP Travel Rule
message is owed).

OnChainSettlementSection.description:
Section B: On-chain settlement data.

Models the four-step lifecycle of an intent on-chain: `submit_tx` (user
deposit / intent creation), `fill_tx` (solver fill on destination chain),
`proof_tx` (cross-chain proof submission), `finalise_tx` (claim/settle on
origin). Oracle + settlement_stage describe the proof-relay layer.

fees.description:
The fees actually charged, as recorded: the venue's own fee report, bridge fees, network
gas the order's wallet paid, and the platform fee. Never a quoted estimate. A fee whose
amount was not reported or could not be read is left out rather than shown as 0, and its
kind is listed in `unrecordedFees`.

fills.description:
Each confirmed fill, in execution order. Always present: empty before any fill is
confirmed.

quotedBuyAmount.description:
The buy amount the executed quote said would land. Null when it is not known (for
example before a venue order is dispatched).

settledBuyAmount.description:
What actually landed, read from the fill or settlement evidence. Null until it is
measured; never the quote carried forward and never 0 for unknown.

settlesBy.description:
The latest time the order settles, or can no longer execute, under its recorded terms:
the signed order's fill deadline, or, on a route, the latest fill deadline every leg
commits to (Advanced); the last on-chain step's send-by time (an on-chain Basic swap).
Null when no such term is recorded, for example a same-chain DEX swap, whose call
carries no deadline.

unrecordedFees.description:
Every fee kind the order incurs whose actual charge is not recorded or could not be
read: a venue fee taken inside the price without an amount, a bridge leg's fee, gas
the order's wallet spent without a readable receipt, a platform fee billed off the
order. Always present; empty only when every incurred charge is in `fees`. An absent
kind with no `fees` line means nothing of that kind was charged. Open set: clients
show an unknown kind generically.

chain.description: The CAIP-2 chain the fee was paid on, for an on-chain charge.

includedInPrice.description:
True when the venue took this fee inside its price: the fill amounts already reflect
it, so it is not charged on top of them.

What a fee paid for.

What the leg quote ESTIMATED this leg would buy. Always the quote: a confirmed
delivery is reported separately in `measuredBuy` rather than overwriting this,
so the two facts stay distinguishable on the wire.

Per-leg counterparty compliance posture — WHO filled this leg and their
regulatory standing. Absent on the generic `OrderResponse`; populated only
on the admin company trade-detail. Lets a composite show "leg 1 = KYB'd
Solver X (Cayman Islands), leg 2 = CCTP protocol" instead of one collapsed
counterparty.

The route quote's per-leg ETA in seconds, when it carried one: the venue's
estimate of this leg's own execution. For a CCTP leg it is the burn-to-mint
upper bound of the chosen finality tier, set by the source chain (Fast ~20 s;
Standard ~19 min from the L1-anchored chains). It never counts the time a
parked route waits for its taker to sign the next leg.

Concrete USD-denominated fee total for this leg. Absent when the route
quote only carried spread/fee bps or a non-USD fee asset.

Normalised leg mechanism: `cctp` | `across` | `relay` | `fx` | `solver`, or the
raw `providerProduct` for a kind the backend does not special-case (clients must
treat this as an open set and fall back to a generic presentation).

recorded for this leg, in the leg's buy asset. Absent until that receipt has
confirmed the leg, which a client must render as "not measured": never as
zero, and never by silently showing `buy` in its place.

This is the only place an INTERMEDIATE leg's real delivery appears. On a
`StableFX -> CCTP` composite the FX leg settles a different asset on a
different chain from the order's own output, so the order-level delivery
cannot describe it.

PairQuote.description:
One venue's quote for the pair. Core price, identity and progress facts are always
present; venue-specific details are omitted when absent. Core timing fields that
do not apply to the quote's firmness remain `null`:

| field | indicative | executable, firm | executable, non-firm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `firm` | false | true | false |
| `expiresAt` | null | set | set |
| `minOut` | null | null | set |
| `observedAt`, `staleAfter` | set | null | null |

A stub (`sources[].priceOnRequest`) is indicative with `null` amounts.

The example is an executable non-firm quote: 10000 USDC paid,
`buy.amount` 9996.0 USDT lands after the included 4.0 USDT provider fee;
`netReceived` 9994.8 also subtracts the 0.0004 ETH network fee the taker pays
separately (`included: false`, about 1.2 USDT at the Reference mid), so it is lower
than `buy.amount`; `minOut` 9966.01 (30 bps) bounds `buy.amount`, not
`netReceived`.

PriceSize.description:
One requested size, with a quote's meanings: `buy` is what lands after every
`included` fee taken in the buy Asset, `netReceived` is for comparison only.

oneOf.description:
The buy amount: the request's on a `buyAmount` read; on a `sellAmount` read, what the sell
amount buys, `null` when nothing could be priced at this size, never `0`.

buy.x-undiscriminated-union-reason: Nullable value: JSON null has no properties and cannot carry a discriminator.

feeObservedAt.description: When the included account commission was observed; display only, not quote consent.

oneOf.description:
The sell amount: the request's on a `sellAmount` read, rounded down to the source's
precision; on a `buyAmount` read, what the buy amount costs, `null` when nothing could be
priced at this size, never `0`.

sell.x-undiscriminated-union-reason: Nullable value: JSON null has no properties and cannot carry a discriminator.

PricesLadderLevel.description: One incremental level: `size` more sell units, each buying `price` buy units.

computedAt.description: When the server built this snapshot (it reuses one for about a second).

oneOf.description: The pair's indicative reference mid, from the same source as POST /quotes. null only when the read failed, with the cause in referenceMidUnavailable; never zero, stale or guessed. Never a quote input.

referenceMid.x-undiscriminated-union-reason: Nullable value: JSON null has no properties and cannot carry a discriminator.

oneOf.description:
Why `referenceMid` is `null`: `marketDataUnavailable` (a market-data refusal or outage),
`notPriced` (no reference price exists for an asset) or `timedOut` (past the read's budget).

referenceMidUnavailable.x-undiscriminated-union-reason: Nullable value: JSON null has no properties and cannot carry a discriminator.

rows.description:
Sorted like quotes: `netReceived` at the first size descending, an unavailable value
last, then by venue id (there is no `best`).

sellBalances.description:
The sell Asset in the caller's own Default-binding wallets, one memory-only read
per deployment (only the pinned chain when `sell.chain` is set). Display only, never a
quote input. Empty for an API key, before the first warm, or with no bound wallet:
unknown, never zero. A client totals the `fresh` entries and names every other entry
as not read, never a silent partial total.

QuoteSourceEntry.description:
One considered venue's outcome, a closed set tagged `status`:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `asking` | in flight on the stream only: the auction is consulting this venue now; its final outcome replaces it under the same venue key, and none remains at `complete` |
| `answered` | the venue produced a quote |
| `needsWallet` | no wallet of `family` to ask with |
| `walletRefused` | the bound wallet is refused (`Revoked`, a confirmed sanctions hit) |
| `firmQuoteLimited` | a desk's firm-quote cap applies; `explanation` is product copy |
| `indicative` | the venue's price is shown without a firm-price ask; `quoteId` identifies the indicative card, whose `firmAsk` says whether the binding price comes on request or at execution |
| `priceOnRequest` | no venue price was requested; `quoteId` identifies the held estimate or stub to Requote |
| `askLimitReached` | the venue's ask limit is reached for now; `retryAfter` says when to ask again |
| `timedOut` | no answer inside the deadline |
| `refused` | the venue refused the live ask |
| `restricted` | a gate kept the venue from this principal |
| `unsupported` | the venue does not serve the pair |
| `filteredOut` | the request's own filters exclude it (never a coverage or chain gap) |
| `unavailable` | a read failed (`admissionUnavailable`, …) |

An unscreened default wallet is not a status: the quote carries `screening`. `venue`
is the venue block, its `id` the one quote legs and `/prices` rows carry. Durations
(`retryAfter`) are ISO 8601, counted from when the response was sent. Every entry
carries `asked`: whether this venue was consulted for this request: a live ask, or a
fresh read of its published book or live desk price within that source's freshness
window. An estimate no venue gave (a model or reference price) is not consulted, and
an `answered` entry is always consulted. How a card's price was obtained is its own
price basis, never this flag.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
Ask for the permission or wallet right `target`. For a member session it is offered only
when the permission-request owner would open (or already holds) a request on it; a target
it refuses by name (`blocked`, `not_applicable`, ...) reads `none`. When that read fails,
the step is offered unchanged.

The calling member's own pending request for this same target (the target key
the create route deduplicates on, so a request made from another venue's card
counts), read once per auction: the member already asked, so a client shows that
instead of offering a second request. Absent when there is none, when the read
failed or timed out (never a guessed value), and always for API keys and
automation principals: only a member session's quotes carry it.

RequoteRequest.description:
Asks the venue of an earlier quote again. Only these fields.

Requote is explicit firm intent, including for a quote originally requested as
`indicative`: every eligible desk is firm-asked under the same authority and limits.
It does not inherit the origin's firmness; non-desk planning is unchanged.

Only that quote's venue (every venue of a multi-leg route) is asked, for the same pair, amount and side,
and the answer is one new held quote with `requoteOf`; the original stays orderable until its own expiry.
A venue's indicative card gets its firm quote this way (every such venue, including one whose
firm quote lives 5 s or less and whose card offers Execute within your limit, `next: order`), like naming
the venue in `filters.venues.include`, under the same desk ask limits. Refusals, each by name: 404
`QUOTE_NOT_FOUND` (unknown or another principal's), 410 `QUOTE_EXPIRED` (over 10 minutes past expiry),
400 `CORRIDOR_NOT_OFFERED`, 403 `SOURCE_NOT_OWNED`,
409 `PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED` (an API key naming a personal wallet), 400 `WALLET_NOT_ON_CHAIN`,
403 `ACCOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE`, 403 `VENUE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIAL`, 409 `REQUOTE_REFUSED` (the venue's
reason in `message`, its token in `details.reason`), 409 `REQUOTE_NEEDS_WALLET`, 504 `REQUOTE_TIMED_OUT`,
429 `QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED` / `VENUE_FIRM_QUOTE_LIMITED` / `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` with `Retry-After`.

api_key.description:
Send the API key in `X-API-Key`.

**Request signing.** A key with signing enabled (enabled for the key in its workspace's credential settings, which return the signing secret once; see [Sign requests](https://docs.tetrafi.io/authentication#sign-requests)) must also sign every request:

- `X-Timestamp`: the current Unix time in seconds, within 300 seconds of the server clock (at most 10 seconds ahead of it on a request that sends `X-Nonce`).
- `X-Nonce`: a fresh random value for each request, 16 to 128 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` and `_` (a UUID fits). Required on a write (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE); optional on a read (GET, HEAD).
- `X-Signature`: lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical string, keyed with the signing secret's 32 bytes (the secret is 64 hex characters; decode it first).

The canonical string is joined by `\n`, with no trailing newline: the `X-Timestamp` value, the `X-Nonce` value, the upper-case method, the path with its query exactly as sent (`/api/v1/orders?limit=1`), and the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes (the SHA-256 of an empty body when there is none). A request without `X-Nonce` (a read) omits the nonce line and signs four lines.

A nonce is accepted once per key: the same nonce again inside the window is refused, whatever the body, so two identical writes in one second each carry their own nonce and both succeed, and a retry signs again with a new nonce. A rate-limited write does not consume its nonce. A read without a nonce changes nothing, so an identical signed read inside the window is admitted again. After a server restart, a signed request with a nonce timestamped at or before 10 seconds after the restart is refused: retry it with a fresh timestamp and nonce.

A signing refusal is a 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED` whose `details.reason` names the cause: `SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` (a header is missing), `SIGNATURE_INVALID` (a malformed header or a wrong signature), `TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NONCE_REQUIRED` (a write without `X-Nonce`), `NONCE_INVALID` (a malformed or repeated `X-Nonce` header), `SIGNATURE_REPLAYED` (the nonce was already accepted) or `SIGNATURE_PREDATES_RESTART` (timestamped before the server restarted). A key at its replay-record bound answers 429 `REPLAY_WINDOW_FULL`.

info.description:
TetraFi is an API for institutional trading across on-chain and off-chain venues: discover assets, request quotes, place an order by quote id and read its status. API keys sign every request.

Asset-pair quotes: every tagged union is tagged by `kind`; only the outcome of `/prices` rows and `sources[]` entries is tagged by `status`.

RateLimit.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.1 structured dictionary, for example `limit=100, remaining=41, reset=19`. Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. get.description: Lists Basic orders using the same envelope as GET /orders/{orderId}. Requires orders_read on an API key, or ViewOrders/PlaceOrder on a session. Newest first by created time and id. A status filter is applied to stored order facts first and then to each order's canonical public status; a filtered page keeps reading until it holds limit items or the orders end, within a bounded scan. A page shorter than limit carries a nextCursor only when that scan reached its limit, and then says so with scanLimitReached: follow nextCursor until null. A cursor is bound to the caller, workspace and exact filters; a malformed, foreign or deleted anchor is INVALID_CURSOR.

get.summary: List the active workspace's Basic and Advanced orders in newest-first order.

post.description: Place an order by the id of a quote you hold (`{quoteId}` from POST /quotes). A Basic venue quote becomes a venue trade (`basicTrade`). Each quote is ordered once: the same quote again answers QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED, and a replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first answer. Read what a quote produced with GET /orders/by-quote/{quoteId}.

parameters.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for API keys (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED); optional for signed-in members. 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. Refusals are not stored: after one, fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

200.description: Order created: a tagged QuoteOrderResponse (`advancedTrade` or `basicTrade`). A Basic trade on an on-chain venue (for example Uniswap v3, paid from an organisation wallet) answers 200 as soon as the order is durable, with `status: working`, before its wallet signs: signing and broadcast run after the answer. Read the order (GET /orders/{orderId}) or subscribe to `order.updated` for its outcome: `settled`, or `unfilled` (terminal) with `operation.dispatch.outcomeCode: not_sent` and `notSentReason: ON_CHAIN_UNSENT` when no swap was sent (an approval may have been mined first, spending its network fee). A refusal before the order exists (limits, compliance, funds, authority) still answers here with its code. A refusal found after the order is claimed but before its wallet is asked (the LP relationship, the venue registry, the audit record or your authority changed) also answers here with its own code, and that order reads `unfilled` with `outcomeCode: not_sent`.

On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

get.summary: Recover the order produced by a held quote

get.description: Returns the latest stored order after a provider refresh. For REST polling, wait 10–15 seconds between reads and honor `Retry-After` on 429; do not poll in a tight loop. After a webhook delivery, perform this GET to obtain the complete current projection. Never put an API key in a URL. Terminality is order-kind dependent: route and atomic venue orders normally complete at `settled`, while claim-based or deferred products may advance to `finalized`.

200.description: Current Basic order. States may be skipped; act on terminal, not on a particular sequence.

get.summary:
Get order status by ID
GET /api/v1/orders/:id - Get order details by ID

post.description: Cancels an undispatched Basic order or a pay-in still awaiting funds. Returns the same order envelope as GET, with status cancelled and terminal true. Repeating cancellation leaves the order unchanged. A durable dispatch claim, a progressed funding leg, or a terminal outcome refuses with ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE and details.status. Requires current PlaceOrder authority; API keys need orders_write and Idempotency-Key. No venue cancellation is attempted.

parameters.description: Required for API keys. Cancellation is naturally idempotent by order id.

post.description: The asset-pair contract uses required `kind: pair` or `kind: requote` to select its strict request body. Missing kind is 400 QUOTE_REQUEST_KIND_REQUIRED; a non-string or unknown kind is 400 QUOTE_REQUEST_KIND_INVALID (details.field is kind). The legacy intent body and shape inference are retired. Validated in order (INVALID_REQUEST naming the field, REQUOTE_FIELDS_CONFLICT, UNKNOWN_ASSET / UNKNOWN_CHAIN / UNKNOWN_VENUE naming the value, ASSET_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a side's Asset has no deployment on the chain pinned for it), INVALID_AMOUNT, SAME_ASSET_NEEDS_CHAIN, CHAIN_PIN_NEEDS_ON_CHAIN, out-of-range INVALID_REQUEST, ROUTING_OPTIONS_FORBIDDEN), then the request_quotes capability, and answered with a PairQuoteSet: every venue planned, venue-hitting plans limited to one every 3 s per principal (429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; cache-only plans are not limited), quotes held for their owner and the set recorded for GET /quotes/requests/{quoteRequestId}. A requote body asks only the earlier quote's venue again (every venue of a multi-leg route, which answers that same route), as JSON (never a stream), and answers a PairQuoteSet whose one quote names it in requoteOf; the earlier quote stays held until its own expiry. Requote refusals: 400 CORRIDOR_NOT_OFFERED / WALLET_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a custody vault or registered workspace address bound to a chain it is not an account of; also on a fresh request), 403 SOURCE_NOT_OWNED / ACCOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE / VENUE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIAL, 404 QUOTE_NOT_FOUND (unknown and another principal's quote alike), 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED (details.reason) / REQUOTE_NEEDS_WALLET / PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED / QUOTE_CANNOT_BE_REFRESHED (a quote recorded before it could be refreshed for a broker's client), 410 REQUOTE_WINDOW_CLOSED (10 minutes after its expiry, past retainUntil; next search: request quotes again), 429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED / VENUE_FIRM_QUOTE_LIMITED /BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After, 503 QUOTE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE / QUOTE_NOT_READY, 504 REQUOTE_TIMED_OUT. Every refusal, at every status, uses the shared ApiError schema. Optional filters narrow the auction. Orderable venue-account cards require a current MFA human Company/Broker session, or an API key holding workspace_venue_trade with its venue switch enabled and HMAC request signing. A member key with quotes_request but no venue-trading authority receives native indicative cards (firm false, expiresAt null) with sourceRefusal venueTradeScopeRequired and a re-issuance remedy, without any firm ask. On-chain sources without an organisation wallet grant are indicative with sourceRefusal onchainWalletNotUsable and a wallet-grant remedy; no signer is resolved. Quote-only observations never spend firm-quote budget, and their held refusal is returned if ordered. An API key quotes with quotes_request (which needs orders_write on the same key); it has no Default wallet of a member, so it selects a trading wallet in source.tradingWallets, a map from CAIP-2 chain to financial-account id (not a wallet address or native wallet id): a workspace custody wallet, or an organisation wallet the key was granted (without that grant the source reads API_KEY_ORGANISATION_WALLET_SCOPE_REQUIRED), never a personal one (409 PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED); its protocol venues remain non-orderable until it binds one; quote-only observations may show a native indicative price without borrowing a wallet. Optional firmness is indicative, firm or auto (absent means auto); unknown values return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with details.field firmness. Indicative never makes a firm desk ask. Firm explicitly asks every eligible desk, with a named source refusal for each desk that cannot be asked, under the existing authority, limits and collection deadline. filters.firmOnly remains a result filter. Requote is renewed explicit firm intent, not inherited indicative intent. In auto, a production desk is firm-asked only by naming it in filters.venues.include or requoting its card; an automatic broad request leaves it indicative or unavailable priceOnRequest when it publishes no price. Its next is requote, except where its firm quote lives 5 s or less: then it is order (execute within my limit), and that order makes the one ask, trading only at or above the person's minReceive; a requote of that card (Get firm quote) also asks it once under the same desk limits and returns a firm, executable card with its expiresAt. A sandbox or testnet desk that publishes nothing is firm-asked on a person's or API caller's request within the desk limits (firmQuoteLimited with retryAfter when they are reached); automation principals get it on requote only. On a venue-account card, top-level deliverTo {kind: address, chain, address, destinationTag?} names where the trade's output is withdrawn when the order for it fills: one of the workspace's own wallets that is an approved withdrawal destination of that venue account, for the receipt asset, with exactly that destination tag or memo. The card then carries that deliverTo, a network fee line for the venue's withdrawal fee (the most the order will pay; a higher fee at send refuses) and a receive net of it (netReceived unavailable withdrawalFeeUnread when the fee could not be read), and a requote keeps it. A venue that cannot deliver there answers its source unavailable with DESTINATION_NOT_APPROVED, DELIVER_TO_NOT_A_WORKSPACE_WALLET, WITHDRAWAL_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED (no withdrawal network for that chain on the site; test sites have none), DELIVER_TO_AMBIGUOUS, WITHDRAWAL_FEE_EXCEEDS_AMOUNT, deliverToCalldataUnsupported or deliverToNotPermitted (deliverTo needs a member session with ViewWallets; an API key lists no deliverTo candidates, and a requote naming one answers 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED with details.reason deliverToNotPermitted). The request spends one Quote token; connection indicative pacing is reported on cards.

200.description: Quotes aggregated successfully: a PairQuoteSet. Accept: text/event-stream selects JSON-data SSE events: quote (PairQuote), source (QuoteSourceEntry), complete (PairQuoteSet), error. A venue the workspace's LP relationship does not allow reads restricted venueRelationship with neutral words in detail and is never asked. Event IDs increase monotonically; the stream includes keepalive comments. Example: broad USD 25000 to USDC, Selini source unavailable accountSetupIncomplete and asked=false; captured live (rfq 2ef31a1ea), one of twelve sources retained, referenceMid omitted and sourceOptions shown empty. No Selini price or firm ask is implied; Selini USD settlement precision is six decimal places.

get.description: The quotes, sources and orders of one asset-pair POST /quotes answer. Required API-key scope: `quotes_read`. Immediate reads use the same held request handed to the asynchronous evidence writer; later reads recover its durable record. Readable by the principal that asked, by a member session with view_orders in its workspace, and by an API key with the additional orders_read scope when an order was placed on one of its quotes in that workspace. Unknown and foreign ids are the same 404. A request lost in a crash before persistence returns 404 QUOTE_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND; its unpersisted quotes are also lost, so request fresh quotes. Genuine store or read failures return retryable 503 QUOTE_REQUEST_UNAVAILABLE with details.retryAfter and Retry-After. requestedByYou says whether the caller asked; only then can it order these quotes.

get.description: Cache-only balance observations across readable workspace wallets and venue accounts. Each wallet accountId is its walletId; venue accounts retain their native venueAccountId. amount is total holdings in exact decimal asset units, asOf is the source observation time, and freshness distinguishes stale or partial observations. No provider request or refresh is started. Accounts without a readable observation are named in unavailable with a cause code, never a fabricated zero. Bank balances are unobservable. Personal wallets are excluded. The wallet resource policy must allow read_balances; venue accounts require current ViewWallets and company/broker or admitted LP authority, exactly as their per-account balance read. Required API-key scope: `treasury_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. Hidden accounts affect neither rows nor cursors. unavailable is repeated on each filtered page. Cursors bind to the workspace, caller, filters and ordered visible row identities; restart if those identities change.

get.description: The one trade history. Projections: scope=workspace (default) reads the workspace's taker orders and venue trades; a member without view_compliance reads only their own, whatever the scope. scope=mine reads the caller's own (a member session only). scope=umbrella reads a broker's clients' orders with each client category's field visibility (view_umbrella_compliance). perspective=maker reads an LP workspace's fills with pseudonymised counterparties (view_settlements); with settlementStage or minAgeSeconds, its unsettled orders by stage (view_bilateral_documents). The default perspective is taker in every workspace. Every row carries tradeId, kind (order or venueTrade) and projection. Page with limit and cursor; format=csv returns the same filtered rows. Accepts a member session or an API key with trades_read; CSV is a member session only.

parameters.description:
mine, workspace or umbrella. Default: workspace. umbrella needs a broker
workspace and view_umbrella_compliance; mine needs a member session.
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description:
taker (default, in every workspace) or maker. maker needs an LP workspace and
view_settlements.
parameters.name: perspective

parameters.description:
all, order or venueTrade. Default: all for taker and umbrella; for maker the
fills default (on-chain orders); umbrella has orders only.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: Settlement status filter, as the projection names it.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description:
Counterparty: the LP's catalogue venue id, the row's `lpVenueId` (taker; a venue
trade matches its execution type's venue) or an LP workspace UUID (orders only), the client workspace (umbrella) or the
taker (maker).
parameters.name: counterpartyId

parameters.description: Exact execution-type identity: the maker of an order (taker), or one of the LP's own venues (maker).
parameters.name: venueId

parameters.description:
The member or client who placed the order: member (taker), user id (umbrella),
entity (maker).
parameters.name: client

parameters.description: Settlement stage of an unsettled order (maker only).
parameters.name: settlementStage

parameters.description: Only orders at least this many seconds old (maker only, with settlementStage).
parameters.name: minAgeSeconds

parameters.description: Placed at or after this RFC 3339 instant (umbrella: a UTC midnight).
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Placed at or before this RFC 3339 instant (umbrella: a UTC midnight).
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Page size; the projection's own bounds apply (default 25).
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: json (default) or csv. csv returns the projection's export of the same filters.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: Taker: comma-separated lifecycle buckets (inProgress, completed, failed, refunded, unknown). Maker: the fills lifecycle filter
parameters.name: lifecycle

parameters.description: Taker: taker, support, counterparty or none
parameters.name: nextActor

parameters.description: Taker: either side's display asset symbol (case-insensitive)
parameters.name: asset

parameters.description: Taker: wallet address (custody vault or linked wallet)

parameters.description: The row's routingPath type: direct or via_broker
parameters.name: routingPath

parameters.description: Field to sort by, as the projection names it
parameters.name: sortBy

parameters.description: Taker: only orders whose nextAction is present
parameters.name: actionRequired

RateLimit.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.1 structured dictionary, for example `limit=100, remaining=41, reset=19`. Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

get.description: Requires current ViewWallets authority in a Company/Broker workspace (or an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the connection holding the account's balance credential, a configured one first (its `connectionId` and execution type are in the body); the observation, staleness and display-value rules are those of the venue-connection balance read, so a balance key held only by a disabled venue returns its last-known balance. 409 VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS for an account whose money is in the company's own wallets, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVERIFY_REQUIRED when no current key holds its balance, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVOKED for a disconnected account, VENUE_ACCOUNT_VENUE_UNKNOWN when its venue is not recognised; 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

get.summary: Read the venue account's balances at its venue

get.description: The account's credit as the Treasury credit card shows it: the provider's reported line (limit, used, available, overrun), the agreed facility, open credit commitments and the signed positions, each with its own observation time. Requires current ViewWallets and ViewCredit authority; an API key or OAuth client additionally needs treasury_read. Figures come from the account's last recorded ledger observation; this read makes no provider call (read the account ledger for a live read). A component that could not be read is `unavailable` with its code, never zero. 403 INSUFFICIENT_WORKSPACE_PERMISSION without ViewCredit; 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, also for another workspace's account; 409 VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS for a wallet-based venue; 503 VENUE_ACCOUNT_ELIGIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE when account access cannot be read.

RateLimit.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.1 structured dictionary, for example `limit=100, remaining=41, reset=19`. RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

get.description: Requires current ViewWallets authority in a Company/Broker workspace (or an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read. Read through the configured connection holding the account's balance credential, with the venue-connection deposit-history rules. Each first answer reads the venue's credit history for `lookbackDays` (1 to 30, default 7), ending now. Optional `limit` (1 to 200) and `cursor` page credits oldest first by observation time and venue deposit id. Follow `nextCursor` until null. A cursor freezes the window and binds its workspace, account, asset, network and complete credit fingerprint; its window takes precedence over lookbackDays. A changed observation refuses the cursor, never skips or repeats a credit. Omit paging for the whole bounded observation. A window holding more than 1,000 records answers no credits with DEPOSIT_HISTORY_WINDOW_TOO_LARGE; read a shorter window. The 409 refusals of the account balance read, plus VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED when only a disabled venue holds the balance key. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

parameters.description:
Initial history window, 1 to 30 days, default 7. On subsequent pages the
cursor's frozen window takes precedence; omit lookbackDays then.
parameters.name: lookbackDays

parameters.description: Credits per page, 1 to 200. Omit for all credits; a cursor retains its page size.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description:
The previous nextCursor. Binds the workspace, account, asset, network,
window and observed credit set. A changed observation refuses instead of skipping credits.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: Read the venue account's deposit history

get.description: Requires current ViewWallets authority in a Company/Broker workspace (or an admitted LP taker). API keys additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the configured connection holding the account's balance credential. Select currency for bank instructions: bankDeposit states available, referenceOnly, notOffered or unread, with a reason and reasonCode. Available receiving coordinates or a reference-only result are in bankInstructions. notOffered comes only from the venue's declared bank offering; failed source reads are unread, never notOffered. The answer is Cache-Control no-store and every receiving-account or full-reference disclosure is audited. The connection read's selection and fee rules apply. Select payInLegId (a summary pay-in window's legId) for one open pay-in leg's payment details: the read uses that leg's currency and, for a dedicated fiat venue, the paying bank its deposit declaration recorded when that bank is linked at the venue; send it alone (400 PAY_IN_LEG_SELECTION_EXCLUSIVE). 404 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_FOUND for a leg that is not this account's pay-in, 409 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_OPEN once it is no longer waiting for funds, 409 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_BANK_CURRENCY for a leg paid in a digital asset (no bank payment details; read the deposit address with asset and chainRef). VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED is answered before any payInLegId is read. The account balance read's 409 refusals also apply, plus VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED when only a disabled venue holds the balance key. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

parameters.description: ISO fiat currency for the bank-deposit read; never with `asset` or `chainRef`.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: The dedicated fiat venue's linked bank id for the sending bank. Required with currency for a dedicated fiat venue and refused for other venues.
parameters.name: providerBankId

parameters.description:
One of the venue account's open pay-in legs (a summary pay-in window's `legId`):
the read selects that leg's currency and, for a dedicated fiat venue, the paying
bank its deposit declaration recorded. Only on the venue-account read, and never

get.summary: Read how to deposit into the venue account

get.description: Reads the account's ledger with current ViewWallets authority. A member session reads the venue live (`source: live`). An API key or OAuth client needs treasury_read and never starts a venue read: it gets the account's last recorded observation (`source: recorded`), dated by `observedAt`, with `stale` true when it is over an hour old, or 409 LEDGER_NOT_OBSERVED when none is recorded yet, and 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND for another workspace's account. Positions and credit retain separate observation and provider times. Failed credit remains unavailable while readable positions are returned. No background polling. 409 LEDGER_UNSUPPORTED means the venue does not report a ledger; LEDGER_SETUP_MISSING means its connection needs setup; VENUE_ACCOUNT_LEDGER_PENDING means the account has not finished setup, so nothing is observed yet. 403 LEDGER_ACCOUNT_FORBIDDEN without View wallets on this workspace's account; foreign accounts refuse before provider I/O. 502 LEDGER_DATA_INVALID when the venue's figures cannot be read as exact amounts; 503 LEDGER_READ_UNAVAILABLE or LEDGER_JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE when the read cannot complete, with the last good read time when one is known. A failed read is never an empty ledger.

get.description: A Company/Broker current human session, or an API key or service account with treasury_read whose principal holds ViewWallets. Each venue account with its venue, where its funds are held, its wallets, linked accounts and execution types, each venue's key state, and whether disabling that venue would retire its key. An account-based item's `accountId` is the `{venueAccountId}` of `GET …/venue-accounts/{venueAccountId}/balances`, `/deposit-history` and `/deposit-instructions`; a walletBased item has no venue account and carries no `accountId` (its `fundingTarget` names the organisation's trading wallets). Key items by `venueEnablementId`. Oldest first, paged by `limit` (default 20, at most 100) and the opaque `cursor` from the previous page's `nextCursor`; `nextCursor` is null on the last page. A foreign or unknown path workspace answers the same 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND without reading that workspace. 400 INVALID_CURSOR for a cursor this list did not issue. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED when the caller's authority to read venue accounts has ended (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission). A session that has itself ended answers 401.

parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from the previous page of the same list and filters.
parameters.name: cursor

Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.

post.description: Rotate a webhook's Standard Webhooks secret. Returns a shown-once whsec_<base64> secret. For 24 hours, webhook-signature carries space-separated v1,<base64> signatures from current and previous decoded keys; either verifies id.timestamp.rawBody. API keys require webhooks_manage and current manage_webhooks permission. Human sessions require manage_webhooks or manage_credentials.

parameters.description: Required for every caller (1 to 255 bytes; missing or empty is 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED). The same key within 24 hours replays the stored 200 without rotating again: secret is null and secretShownOnce true. A new key rotates again. Reuse with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

Remaining is the admitted decision's headroom; reset is whole seconds until quota next becomes available, not an epoch or a promise of a full burst refill. On a limiter's 429 remaining is 0 and reset equals Retry-After. Accepted key, route and per-address policies are compared by lowest remaining, then longest reset. A venue refusal without a known quota makes no rate-limit header claim.

RateLimit-Policy.description: draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-07 section 3.5: quota and window in seconds, for example `100;w=60`. Sent on every status when a finite limiter counted the request. The applicable policy closest to exhaustion is reported (section 3.2): lowest remaining, then longest reset. On a limiter's 429 this is exactly the policy that refused; if a venue discloses no quota, the headers are absent.
